Nightmare Nightclub

By: Graham Coetzer | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Hatfield Strip is an area frequented by young people looking for a fun night out - but one nightclub has a notorious reputation for its brutal bouncers and underage drinking. With many raising con

Unique Selling Point:
We've been approached by a loose knit group of individuals who are all very concerned about the goings on at the notorious Latino's Bistro, a nightclub operating in an area known as the Hatfield Strip in Pretoria. The individuals include members of an NPO working against human trafficking, private security, the Brooklyn CPF and a local ward councillor. They say Latino's has a reputation for underage drinking, young girls having their drinks spiked, brutal bouncers and staff members who have less than savory backgrounds. Sources they've provided have given us CCTV footage pointing to an alleged murder that happened at the club(two staff members who were arrested at the time have seemingly gotten off scott free), and a staff member being implicated in the rape of a 16 year-old girl, amongst others. Behind it all, owner and Algerian citizen Kasi "Pascal" Nacer.

Summary:
Behind the glittering lights and seemingly never-ending party scene at nightclubs in the Hatfield area, lurks hidden dangers for the young people looking for a good time in many of the area's nightclubs. In a gritty look at what lies just beneath the surface of a supposedly glamorous nightlife, we expose how no attempt is being made to protect young people from the often violent and sordid streets of Pretoria.

Further information:
Except for the CCTV footage and two main cases of rape and murder, we've also been given documentary evidence that Pascal is evading tax with many of his businesses. We can also connect him to the criminal underworld through known associates, one of them a staff member at Latinos: Renier van den Vyfer, who used to be a business associate of Nafiz Modack (currently on trial for the murder of Charl Kinnear) and was also arrested for intimidating police investigating Kinnear's murder.
We have hidden camera footage of the club at night, as well as many social media posts, showing what appears to be underage drinkers.
Our main voices:
Parents of 16 year old rape victim - hidden ID
Jarad Frimmel - ward councillor, has responded to many of the incidents of violence at the club. Was at the scene the night of the murder - Hidden ID
Werner Beineke - CPF member who has responded to many of the scenes of violence and alleged drink spiking. Was present at the rape case
Bronwen Davies - Forensic Toxicologist and Lecturer at UCT - Has conducted one of the few decent studies into drug related sexual assault and has wealth of info on the topic
Elton Davies - Father of a young man who posted about on tiktok about the violence at Latino's. His son was apparently kidnapped by Renier and others, beaten up and threatened, and this all on Pascal's orders, who was watching it on a video call.
Sanet Dippenaar from Muelmed Hospital in PTA CBD - one of the nearest private hospitals to Latinos. Has confirmed the receive about 2 cases of drink spiking every weekend, and usually at least one during the week. A lot of these come from Nightclubs in PTA area.

Script:


Nightmare Nightclub
Final Script
16 June 2023


Upsound Music and CCTV

Voice
In a dark and deserted alley, a man paces up and down, helpless to save a fatally wounded friend.

He’s made a rudimentary bandage and frantically looks around for assistance.

Moments later, his friend lies dead on the pavement.

Voice - opening
It’s a narrow row of buildings, spanning the length of a street block in Hatfield, Pretoria.

It comes to life as night falls and the city empties of office workers, replaced by students in search of loud music and cheap drinks.

Gaudy signs light up, the bars and clubs open their doors, and the partying begins.

The city’s entertainment hotspot, it’s known simply as “The Strip”.  

Link Lourensa
But hidden just below the surface of the neon lights and vibrant nightlife lurks a much darker side to the story. A place with a reputation so notorious, some have called it Pretoria’s Nightmare Nightclub.

Upsound Comments and show on screen
My one friend got stabbed and has 10 staples in his head
One of the bouncers attacked a guy outside the restaurant with a chain while the owner looked on.

Upsound Jarad Frimmel
“…all these cases are linked to Latinos. Why is there no investigation, why is there no follow up?

Upsound Mark
Stay away. If you love your life, yes it’s cool to go clubbing but do it in an other place where it’s safe.

Upsound TIKTOK “A NIGHT ON THE STRIP” Fight scenes

Voice
Violence is common across the strip. Brawls fueled by a toxic mix of testosterone and cheap liquor; police are an almost constant presence. But, even here, this club stands out: the dreaded Latino’s Bistro.



Voice
It’s right in the middle of the strip, a prime location with a sordid reputation.

Upsound Matthew
Anything that can happen, does happen at Latinos

Voice
It’s owned by this man, Nacer “Pascal” Kaci. In our time on The Strip we hear that he rules with an iron fist. With help from a team of often violent bouncers.

And these images are allegedly examples of their handiwork.

For protection, this man asked us to hide his identity. We’ll call him Matthew. He’s witnessed the violence and chaos Latino’s has developed a reputation for.

Upsound Matthew
Lourensa: So tell us about Pascal?

Matthew: Ok, so Pascal is originally from Algeria, he came here in South Africa a few years ago, and he’s married to a South African lady.

Lourensa: What kind of an establishment is Latinos Bistro?

Matthew: So you go there to drink, or you go there to party, I can’t say where or how you’ll end up being the next day.

SoundUp Latinos TIKTOK

Voice
It’s an image at odds with what’s portrayed online.

SoundUp Latinos TIKTOK

Link Lourensa
The posts paint a pretty picture but take a deeper dive into social media and you’ll find dozens of complaints about Latinos. And they reveal an altogether more sinister side to club.

Voice
But finding people willing to speak out – to shed light on how and why the club has such a fearsome reputation – is hard. Few appear willing to take the risk. This man, who we’ll call Mark, isn’t surprised.

Upsound “Mark”
Lourensa: There are many clubs on the strip, what makes Latinos stand out?

Mark: Well mostly it’s the assault and the fighting. The bouncer throwing out someone and beating them senseless until there’s no movement. Or you’ll see students just arguing under each other, and then next moment the bouncers will come in or the Latinos staff will come in and just beat everyone, just for the fun of it, of beating someone.

Upsound Comments and show on screen
Please be warned! Spiking of drinks occur at this venue! It is NOT SAFE!
Very unsafe and dangerous

Voice
Just a few weeks ago, Mark says he saw a patron brutally attacked by Latinos staff, while Pascal looked on.

Upsound “Mark”
they started just beating this one guy. Started beating him, then they stabbed him, there was lots of blood. I will never forget the amount of blood on that scene.

Voice
Onlookers, including Mark, were convinced the man was bleeding to death. Not that his attackers appeared to care.

UPSOUND “MARK”
And they just left him there on the side of the road and walked off as if nothing happened. Luckily an ambulance arrived fast, and they took the guy, and I literally think they saved his life.

Link Lourensa
This wasn’t an easy story to tell. We’ve uncovered allegations of drugs, rape and even murder at Latinos. No wonder then that many of the victims we’ve spoken to were simply too scared to come on camera, even when we offered to hide their identities.

Voice
But Jarad Frimmel refused to be silenced. He’s a local ward councillor.

Upsound Jarad Frimmel
Going to Latino’s, they say their children walk in, they want to go and have a drink or socialise, and they’re intimidated by the bouncers, they’re intimidated by the people who work behind the bar. And all they say they’re doing is they say they look at them funny, or they bump into them. And now suddenly they get assaulted or they get thrown out of the club.

Voice
But, as our investigation uncovered, those are the lucky ones.

Voice - CCTV 
It’s Sunday the 29th of May, 2022. This leaked CCTV footage is from a camera mounted outside Latinos’ front entrance. Two men are pushed through a crowd and into the club. It’s 00:41 in the morning.
The first man is held around his neck. He’s been stabbed in the leg and is bleeding profusely.

A police statement would later claim his attackers are unknown and that he was stabbed in the street a short distance from the club. It’s not known why the victim, as well as a man who appears to be his friend, were taken into the club. Behind them is a bouncer who works for Latinos.

It’s the start of an incident that ends in tragedy and remains a mystery to this day.

Upsound Matthew
So Latinos has got quite a few bouncers. You’ve got these very, very big guys. So you’ll always see them outside the front of Latinos. And whenever there’s violence you’ll see them involved. I mean I’ve personally seen them kicking someone whilst the person is unconscious on the floor.

Voice
This camera captures an alleyway behind Latinos. It runs the length of the strip and is deserted.

At 00:43, two of the men who allegedly dragged the stabbing victim and his friend into the club, are seen leaving through a back door. They’re with a security guard who arrived in the alleyway a few minutes earlier.

Upsound Matthew
Now the two people that brought the victims in are walking away the back alley, walking down away from Latinos.

Voice
Seconds later, the stabbing victim is dragged into the alley by the bouncer seen following them earlier.

Upsound Matthew
In this footage you see Pascal, and that’s with the second victim, he’s talking to him. And then Pascal goes inside.

Voice
Apart from his companion, there appears no interest in helping the wounded man.

Upsound Matthew
Lourensa: Looks like he’s pleading with him.

Matthew: Correct.

Voice
Ignoring the pleas, the gathered men appear anxious to get rid of the blood.

Upsound Matthew
Matthew: Now they’ve got a hose, and they’re washing away the blood from inside latinos.

Lourensa: You can see the trail of blood leading to the body as well.

Matthew: Correct. And now they’re attempting to just simply wash it away.

Voice
It’s not the only incident that’s brought us here. Latino’s reputation extends beyond moments of unbridled violence, and our investigation reveals why.

Upsound Comments and show on screen
-They sell alcohol to under age kids and aren't bothered.
- underage children always manages to get in

Link Lourensa
Drink spiking, date rape drugs, we’ve all read the headlines. But for one mother, what she’d only previously seen in the news, became a horrific reality earlier this year.

Voice
Worried about the consequences of speaking out, we’ve hidden her identity and called her Sandra.

Upsound “Sandra”
Mary: She’s a typical teenager. She’s quite sporty. And she loves socialising with her friends.

Voice
Sandra’s teenaged daughter was supposed to be at a sleepover. But, she and her friends had made their way to Latino’s instead.

Upsound “Sandra”
So they went without our permission, our knowledge that evening. They got in there somehow, I’m not sure how they were let in. And they were given alcohol, or they bought alcohol.

Voice
Tragically, a fun night out ended in trauma.

Upsound “Sandra”
Her drink was spiked, and after she got separated from her friend, she was taken to a location close by, and she was sexually assaulted. 

Voice
Her daughter remembers very little about that night, but sometime after 10pm she became another statistic, allegedly drugged and raped.

Voice
We obtained CCTV footage showing Sandra’s daughter arriving at a nearby guesthouse. Witnesses say she’d left the club with an adult male who, it’s alleged, is often seen at Latinos.

And it’s here, drifting in and out of consciousness, that she claims she was raped.

Despite telling her parents, she chose not to report the assault to the police.

Upsound “Sandra”
She’s definitely anxious and scared, she’s told me that she knows that they are dangerous people.

Upsound Jarad Frimmel
Lourensa: If we look at the Brooklyn Police Station, can you tell us a bit about the crime statistics, how some of these serious cases are investigated and do they ever go to court?

Jarad: So there’s a high number of cases of rape, of common assault, common robbery, assault GBH, all of these different cases have been opened. But then when you speak to some of the victims, and you try and say well have you been assisted, is your case being investigated, they come back and they say no they’re not getting any assistance. Or the case is still being investigated, two years down the line.

Voice
And there’s no better evidence of that than the events of that Sunday morning in May, 2022.

At 00:51, eight minutes after being dragged into the alleyway, the wounded man’s pants are removed by his friend who uses them to make a tourniquet to try and stem the bleeding.

For the next 21 minutes, the victim is clearly in agony.

When help eventually arrives at 01:16, he is dead.

Police from Brooklyn later arrested one of the bouncers and the security guard. They were charged with murder and defeating the ends of justice. But both were later released and the case has stalled.

This picture, allegedly taken inside Latinos that night, was widely shared on social media.

Upsound Comments and show on screen
This club is run by a gang.

Voice
Pascal declined an interview but, in a letter from his attorneys, strongly denied all the allegations against him and Latinos staff, including that underage persons are allowed in and are sold alcohol, or that an incident of spiking and sexual harassment happened on his premises. Nor, he says, was he, his staff, or management made aware of the allegation.

On the stabbing incident and events captured in the alleyway, Pascal says his management assisted the Brooklyn SAPS with information and in identifying the suspect.

He says one of his bouncers called an ambulance and, in trying to assist the victims, was arrested. The NPA declined to prosecute and he was released.

Link Lourensa
So are the police doing enough to protect youngsters visiting place like Latinos? We asked them for an interview but they declined.

Voice
In a written response, the police said most of the cases reported at Latino’s between January and May this year have involved charges and counter-charges between patrons and bouncers. All suspects were arrested and appeared in court.
  


But Matthew says those are only the cases the police are aware of.

Sound Up Matthew
…They are so afraid… They are so afraid of repercussions by Latinos, that they simply, they don’t want to go to the police.

Voice
Despite what the police told us, Pascal said none of his staff were aware of any attacks on Latino’s patrons, and denied that either he or his members were party to it.

Voice
With the beats of nearby nightlife echoing in the distance, we took one last drive along the back of The Strip.

Link Lourensa
So this is the alley where John Doe died, this is what it looks like at night. No place to spend the last moments of your life alone, and in pain.

ENDS

He’s made a rudimentary bandage and frantically looks around for assistance. Moments later, his friend lies dead on the pavement. Voice - opening It’s a narrow row of buildings, spanning the length of a street block in Hatfield, Pretoria. It comes to life as night falls and the city empties of office workers, replaced by students in search of loud music and cheap drinks. Gaudy signs light up, the bars and clubs open their doors, and the partying begins. The city’s entertainment hotspot, it’s known simply as “The Strip”. Link Lourensa But hidden just below the surface of the neon lights and vibrant nightlife lurks a much darker side to the story. A place with a reputation so notorious, some have called it Pretoria’s Nightmare Nightclub. Upsound Comments and show on screen My one friend got stabbed and has 10 staples in his head One of the bouncers attacked a guy outside the restaurant with a chain while the owner looked on. Upsound Jarad Frimmel “…all these cases are linked to Latinos. Why is there no investigation, why is there no follow up? Upsound Mark Stay away. If you love your life, yes it’s cool to go clubbing but do it in an other place where it’s safe. Upsound TIKTOK “A NIGHT ON THE STRIP” Fight scenes Voice Violence is common across the strip. Brawls fueled by a toxic mix of testosterone and cheap liquor; police are an almost constant presence. But, even here, this club stands out: the dreaded Latino’s Bistro. Voice It’s right in the middle of the strip, a prime location with a sordid reputation. Upsound Matthew Anything that can happen, does happen at Latinos Voice It’s owned by this man, Nacer “Pascal” Kaci. In our time on The Strip we hear that he rules with an iron fist. With help from a team of often violent bouncers. And these images are allegedly examples of their handiwork. For protection, this man asked us to hide his identity. We’ll call him Matthew. He’s witnessed the violence and chaos Latino’s has developed a reputation for. Upsound Matthew Lourensa: So tell us about Pascal? Matthew: Ok, so Pascal is originally from Algeria, he came here in South Africa a few years ago, and he’s married to a South African lady. Lourensa: What kind of an establishment is Latinos Bistro? Matthew: So you go there to drink, or you go there to party, I can’t say where or how you’ll end up being the next day. SoundUp Latinos TIKTOK Voice It’s an image at odds with what’s portrayed online. SoundUp Latinos TIKTOK Link Lourensa The posts paint a pretty picture but take a deeper dive into social media and you’ll find dozens of complaints about Latinos. And they reveal an altogether more sinister side to club. Voice But finding people willing to speak out – to shed light on how and why the club has such a fearsome reputation – is hard. Few appear willing to take the risk. This man, who we’ll call Mark, isn’t surprised. Upsound “Mark” Lourensa: There are many clubs on the strip, what makes Latinos stand out? Mark: Well mostly it’s the assault and the fighting. The bouncer throwing out someone and beating them senseless until there’s no movement. Or you’ll see students just arguing under each other, and then next moment the bouncers will come in or the Latinos staff will come in and just beat everyone, just for the fun of it, of beating someone. Upsound Comments and show on screen Please be warned! Spiking of drinks occur at this venue! It is NOT SAFE! Very unsafe and dangerous Voice Just a few weeks ago, Mark says he saw a patron brutally attacked by Latinos staff, while Pascal looked on. Upsound “Mark” they started just beating this one guy. Started beating him, then they stabbed him, there was lots of blood. I will never forget the amount of blood on that scene. Voice Onlookers, including Mark, were convinced the man was bleeding to death. Not that his attackers appeared to care. UPSOUND “MARK” And they just left him there on the side of the road and walked off as if nothing happened. Luckily an ambulance arrived fast, and they took the guy, and I literally think they saved his life. Link Lourensa This wasn’t an easy story to tell. We’ve uncovered allegations of drugs, rape and even murder at Latinos. No wonder then that many of the victims we’ve spoken to were simply too scared to come on camera, even when we offered to hide their identities. Voice But Jarad Frimmel refused to be silenced. He’s a local ward councillor. Upsound Jarad Frimmel Going to Latino’s, they say their children walk in, they want to go and have a drink or socialise, and they’re intimidated by the bouncers, they’re intimidated by the people who work behind the bar. And all they say they’re doing is they say they look at them funny, or they bump into them. And now suddenly they get assaulted or they get thrown out of the club. Voice But, as our investigation uncovered, those are the lucky ones. Voice - CCTV It’s Sunday the 29th of May, 2022. This leaked CCTV footage is from a camera mounted outside Latinos’ front entrance. Two men are pushed through a crowd and into the club. It’s 00:41 in the morning. The first man is held around his neck. He’s been stabbed in the leg and is bleeding profusely. A police statement would later claim his attackers are unknown and that he was stabbed in the street a short distance from the club. It’s not known why the victim, as well as a man who appears to be his friend, were taken into the club. Behind them is a bouncer who works for Latinos. It’s the start of an incident that ends in tragedy and remains a mystery to this day. Upsound Matthew So Latinos has got quite a few bouncers. You’ve got these very, very big guys. So you’ll always see them outside the front of Latinos. And whenever there’s violence you’ll see them involved. I mean I’ve personally seen them kicking someone whilst the person is unconscious on the floor. Voice This camera captures an alleyway behind Latinos. It runs the length of the strip and is deserted. At 00:43, two of the men who allegedly dragged the stabbing victim and his friend into the club, are seen leaving through a back door. They’re with a security guard who arrived in the alleyway a few minutes earlier. Upsound Matthew Now the two people that brought the victims in are walking away the back alley, walking down away from Latinos. Voice Seconds later, the stabbing victim is dragged into the alley by the bouncer seen following them earlier. Upsound Matthew In this footage you see Pascal, and that’s with the second victim, he’s talking to him. And then Pascal goes inside. Voice Apart from his companion, there appears no interest in helping the wounded man. Upsound Matthew Lourensa: Looks like he’s pleading with him. Matthew: Correct. Voice Ignoring the pleas, the gathered men appear anxious to get rid of the blood. Upsound Matthew Matthew: Now they’ve got a hose, and they’re washing away the blood from inside latinos. Lourensa: You can see the trail of blood leading to the body as well. Matthew: Correct. And now they’re attempting to just simply wash it away. Voice It’s not the only incident that’s brought us here. Latino’s reputation extends beyond moments of unbridled violence, and our investigation reveals why. Upsound Comments and show on screen -They sell alcohol to under age kids and aren't bothered. - underage children always manages to get in Link Lourensa Drink spiking, date rape drugs, we’ve all read the headlines. But for one mother, what she’d only previously seen in the news, became a horrific reality earlier this year. Voice Worried about the consequences of speaking out, we’ve hidden her identity and called her Sandra. Upsound “Sandra” Mary: She’s a typical teenager. She’s quite sporty. And she loves socialising with her friends. Voice Sandra’s teenaged daughter was supposed to be at a sleepover. But, she and her friends had made their way to Latino’s instead. Upsound “Sandra” So they went without our permission, our knowledge that evening. They got in there somehow, I’m not sure how they were let in. And they were given alcohol, or they bought alcohol. Voice Tragically, a fun night out ended in trauma. Upsound “Sandra” Her drink was spiked, and after she got separated from her friend, she was taken to a location close by, and she was sexually assaulted. Voice Her daughter remembers very little about that night, but sometime after 10pm she became another statistic, allegedly drugged and raped. Voice We obtained CCTV footage showing Sandra’s daughter arriving at a nearby guesthouse. Witnesses say she’d left the club with an adult male who, it’s alleged, is often seen at Latinos. And it’s here, drifting in and out of consciousness, that she claims she was raped. Despite telling her parents, she chose not to report the assault to the police. Upsound “Sandra” She’s definitely anxious and scared, she’s told me that she knows that they are dangerous people. Upsound Jarad Frimmel Lourensa: If we look at the Brooklyn Police Station, can you tell us a bit about the crime statistics, how some of these serious cases are investigated and do they ever go to court? Jarad: So there’s a high number of cases of rape, of common assault, common robbery, assault GBH, all of these different cases have been opened. But then when you speak to some of the victims, and you try and say well have you been assisted, is your case being investigated, they come back and they say no they’re not getting any assistance. Or the case is still being investigated, two years down the line. Voice And there’s no better evidence of that than the events of that Sunday morning in May, 2022. At 00:51, eight minutes after being dragged into the alleyway, the wounded man’s pants are removed by his friend who uses them to make a tourniquet to try and stem the bleeding. For the next 21 minutes, the victim is clearly in agony. When help eventually arrives at 01:16, he is dead. Police from Brooklyn later arrested one of the bouncers and the security guard. They were charged with murder and defeating the ends of justice. But both were later released and the case has stalled. This picture, allegedly taken inside Latinos that night, was widely shared on social media. Upsound Comments and show on screen This club is run by a gang. Voice Pascal declined an interview but, in a letter from his attorneys, strongly denied all the allegations against him and Latinos staff, including that underage persons are allowed in and are sold alcohol, or that an incident of spiking and sexual harassment happened on his premises. Nor, he says, was he, his staff, or management made aware of the allegation. On the stabbing incident and events captured in the alleyway, Pascal says his management assisted the Brooklyn SAPS with information and in identifying the suspect. He says one of his bouncers called an ambulance and, in trying to assist the victims, was arrested. The NPA declined to prosecute and he was released. Link Lourensa So are the police doing enough to protect youngsters visiting place like Latinos? We asked them for an interview but they declined. Voice In a written response, the police said most of the cases reported at Latino’s between January and May this year have involved charges and counter-charges between patrons and bouncers. All suspects were arrested and appeared in court. But Matthew says those are only the cases the police are aware of. Sound Up Matthew …They are so afraid… They are so afraid of repercussions by Latinos, that they simply, they don’t want to go to the police. Voice Despite what the police told us, Pascal said none of his staff were aware of any attacks on Latino’s patrons, and denied that either he or his members were party to it. Voice With the beats of nearby nightlife echoing in the distance, we took one last drive along the back of The Strip. Link Lourensa So this is the alley where John Doe died, this is what it looks like at night. No place to spend the last moments of your life alone, and in pain. ENDS PROMO1 VO The gaudy lights and loud music attracts the crowds - but beneath this shiny veneer lurks PRETORIA’S dark underbelly of underage drinking and violence. Upsound Sound Up Mark …They are so afraid… they are so afraid of repercussions that they simply, don’t want to go to the police. VO On the strip - we uncover the details of a mysterious death… PROMO3 VO Underage drinking and brawls fuelled by cheap alcohol - familiar scenes at a hotspot frequented by young people in search of a good time. Upsound Jarad Frimmel “… Why is there no investigation, why is there no follow up?” VO But one night club stands out for violent street fights and risky business.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: We've been approached by a loose knit group of individuals who are all very concerned about the goings on at the notorious Latino's Bistro, a nightclub operating in an area known as the Hatfield Strip in Pretoria. The individuals include members of an NPO working against human trafficking, private security, the Brooklyn CPF and a local ward councillor. They say Latino's has a reputation for underage drinking, young girls having their drinks spiked, brutal bouncers and staff members who have less than savory backgrounds. Sources they've provided have given us CCTV footage pointing to an alleged murder that happened at the club(two staff members who were arrested at the time have seemingly gotten off scott free), and a staff member being implicated in the rape of a 16 year-old girl, amongst others. Behind it all, owner and Algerian citizen Kasi "Pascal" Nacer.
metadata.Summary: Behind the glittering lights and seemingly never-ending party scene at nightclubs in the Hatfield area, lurks hidden dangers for the young people looking for a good time in many of the area's nightclubs. In a gritty look at what lies just beneath the surface of a supposedly glamorous nightlife, we expose how no attempt is being made to protect young people from the often violent and sordid streets of Pretoria.
metadata.Further information: Except for the CCTV footage and two main cases of rape and murder, we've also been given documentary evidence that Pascal is evading tax with many of his businesses. We can also connect him to the criminal underworld through known associates, one of them a staff member at Latinos: Renier van den Vyfer, who used to be a business associate of Nafiz Modack (currently on trial for the murder of Charl Kinnear) and was also arrested for intimidating police investigating Kinnear's murder. We have hidden camera footage of the club at night, as well as many social media posts, showing what appears to be underage drinkers. Our main voices: Parents of 16 year old rape victim - hidden ID Jarad Frimmel - ward councillor, has responded to many of the incidents of violence at the club. Was at the scene the night of the murder - Hidden ID Werner Beineke - CPF member who has responded to many of the scenes of violence and alleged drink spiking. Was present at the rape case Bronwen Davies - Forensic Toxicologist and Lecturer at UCT - Has conducted one of the few decent studies into drug related sexual assault and has wealth of info on the topic Elton Davies - Father of a young man who posted about on tiktok about the violence at Latino's. His son was apparently kidnapped by Renier and others, beaten up and threatened, and this all on Pascal's orders, who was watching it on a video call. Sanet Dippenaar from Muelmed Hospital in PTA CBD - one of the nearest private hospitals to Latinos. Has confirmed the receive about 2 cases of drink spiking every weekend, and usually at least one during the week. A lot of these come from Nightclubs in PTA area.
